paragraphs: Boostlingo sells language access services along with the software to run them, helping organizations communicate across languages by combining human interpreters and AI. Interpreting, translation and multilingual events sit together on one platform.

For on-demand work a user selects a language, requests an interpreter and starts a session by phone or video without an appointment. The company states access to more than 17,000 human interpreters across over 300 languages. AI interpreting covers 23 languages and can roll over to human interpreters. Behind the sessions sits a management system for interpreter scheduling, routing, credentials, rate management, billing and reporting.

The company names healthcare systems, public agencies, schools, nonprofits, businesses and language service providers among the teams it serves. Interpreters are said to need a minimum of three years of experience. The site describes SOC 2 Type II compliance and HIPAA-compliant workflows for secure interpreting.

quote.text: Use AI where it fits. Human interpreters when it counts.
